title: Windsurfing
coreMove: Shrink a condition-shaped skill to one live subskill that can be repeated safely and then tested by the real environment.
sourcePressure: The source frames windsurfing as environment-shaped practice where staged isolation of subskills and risk-aware progression make a condition-dependent skill trainable.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Using staging to avoid the real environment instead of using it to make one live piece of the environment readable and safer.

sourceAnchors.name: windsurfing
sourceAnchors.detail: the frozen support names windsurfing as the final case and frames it through conditions, equipment, and staged risk
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Windsurfing refuses to be learned only in your head because wind, board, sail, and water keep changing the assignment.

sourceAnchors.name: staged isolation of subskills
sourceAnchors.detail: the source says staged isolation of subskills helps make windsurfing trainable while risk-aware progression matters because conditions cannot be fully controlled
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A staged subskill is honest only if it is still on speaking terms with wind and water.

exampleSpecs.domain: kayak rescue-club edging drill in a sheltered cove
exampleSpecs.audience: a learner whose water skill needs live but bounded conditions
exampleSpecs.stakes: open-water practice is unsafe until edge recovery stops surprising him
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Sam stays in the sheltered cove, repeats one edge-and-recover sequence beside the instructor boat, then tests it once where the current begins to tug
exampleSpecs.firstImage: green water tapping against a kayak blade near a buoy line

exampleSpecs.domain: drone pilot learning crosswind landing in a marked field
exampleSpecs.audience: a technical outdoor learner whose conditions change the assignment
exampleSpecs.stakes: a client shoot fails if the drone drifts into trees during landing
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Margaux predicts simulator time is enough, then isolates only crosswind landings between two field cones before flying near the tree line
exampleSpecs.firstImage: two orange cones trembling in a gust across short grass

exampleSpecs.domain: ski patrol trainee practicing loaded sled turns on a low slope
exampleSpecs.audience: a learner in a risky outdoor skill needing staged progression
exampleSpecs.stakes: a full run with a loaded sled could endanger both trainee and patient
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Ryan chooses the low slope, repeats only the loaded turn with a trainer walking beside him, and advances after the sled stops fishtailing
exampleSpecs.firstImage: red sled straps laid across packed spring snow

exampleSpecs.domain: outdoor photographer learning manual exposure in changing cloud cover
exampleSpecs.audience: a creator whose practice must answer to moving conditions
exampleSpecs.stakes: a paid family session will lose the faces whenever clouds break and return
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Catarina stops practicing every camera setting, isolates exposure changes every time a cloud crosses the sun, and checks the histogram after each five-shot set
exampleSpecs.firstImage: cloud shadow sliding over a white reflector on damp grass

exampleSpecs.domain: outdoor market vendor learning canopy setup in wind
exampleSpecs.audience: a practical learner whose equipment and conditions interact
exampleSpecs.stakes: one loose canopy leg can damage neighboring stalls before opening
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Luke asks the experienced vendor to isolate the windward-leg sequence, repeats it with empty weights first, then tests it when gusts hit the aisle
exampleSpecs.firstImage: canvas snapping against a half-weighted canopy leg

exampleSpecs.domain: field archaeologist learning total-station setup on uneven ground
exampleSpecs.audience: a learner in a condition-sensitive technical field task
exampleSpecs.stakes: bad leveling ruins the day's grid points before the trench team starts
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Adaeze narrows the session to leveling the tripod on uneven ground, repeats it beside one trench, and lets the morning's first grid reading judge whether it held
exampleSpecs.firstImage: your boot pressing into chalky soil beside three tripod feet

skillTargets: choose staged isolation without avoiding real conditions
identify which environmental variable changes the practice task
evaluate safe progression from sheltered subskill to live test
distinguish equipment detail from trainable condition-shaped behavior
